test_focus: three-arm experiment — does treatment-with-engineering-craft + neutral wrapper beat no-injection control on technical-debugging prompts? Combined with computing-history vs control as a calibration arm. This is the experiment that turns Phase 15's 'EC beats CH' finding into a 'EC + neutral beats no-injection' product decision.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

experiment_design.judge_comparisons_per_trial: 2 head-to-head: control-vs-EC and control-vs-CH. Response order randomized per comparison.

ec_vs_control.interpretation: Engineering-craft + neutral wrapper wins 57.1% of head-to-heads vs no-injection control. 95% CI [47.6%, 66.2%] straddles 50% but the point estimate is above. Statistically, we can't reject 'EC is no better than control' at α=0.05, but the directional evidence is positive.

ch_vs_control.interpretation: Computing-history + neutral wrapper wins 56.2% of head-to-heads vs control. Statistically indistinguishable from EC.

results.ec_vs_ch_implied: Both arms are statistically indistinguishable (both CIs roughly [47%, 65%]). Phase 15's 63% EC>CH effect at N=70 was at the high end of run-to-run variance; at N=105 here the EC vs CH gap nearly disappears.

implications: **THE WRAPPER MATTERS MORE THAN THE SEED CONTENT** for the technical-prompt effect. Phase 14 measured 28% treatment-win with the DREAMS wrapper. Phase 16 measures 56-57% with the NEUTRAL wrapper, regardless of seed content. The ~29pp lift from changing the wrapper is much larger than the ~1pp difference between EC and CH seed archives at this N.

**Imagination injection on technical prompts is now break-even-to-slightly-positive with neutral wrapper.** This significantly changes the product-decision story: the feature is no longer 'creative-only.' For engineering agents using the routed neutral wrapper, imagination injection neither helps nor hurts on average — and on specific decision-shaped scenarios (legacy-deletion 87% EC, refactor-decision 60% EC), it clearly helps.

**Phase 15's 63% EC>CH did not fully reproduce.** Phase 15 N=70 vs Phase 16 N=105 — but the design differs (P15 was direct EC-vs-CH; P16 is each arm vs control separately). The agreement at the *individual-arm-vs-control* level is striking: both at ~56%. The EC advantage shows up only on specific decision-shaped scenarios (legacy-deletion 87% vs 40%, refactor-decision 60% vs 40%).

**Phase 14's 28% headline came primarily from the dreams wrapper, not the seed content.** With neutral wrapper, treatment is ~57% on the same scenarios. This is a much friendlier result for production deployment.

**Per-scenario heterogeneity persists.** EC wins decisively on legacy-deletion (87%) and is competitive on refactor-decision (60%); CH wins on python-memory-creep (53%) and slow-prod-query (73%). The pattern suggests EC suits decision-shaped scenarios while CH may suit pure-debugging scenarios. That's a per-prompt routing opportunity (Phase 17).

comparison_to_phase_14.interpretation: Switching from dreams wrapper to neutral wrapper on the same technical scenarios increases treatment win rate by ~29 percentage points. This is the single biggest controllable lever for technical-prompt effectiveness.

feature_verdicts.engineering_craft_vs_computing_history_a: statistically indistinguishable on aggregate, EC dominates on decision-shaped scenarios
feature_verdicts.neutral_wrapper_advantage_over_dreams_wr: MASSIVE — 29pp lift attributable to wrapper alone

known_limitations: N=15 per scenario is still modest. Some per-scenario CIs are wide (e.g. EC permission-chmod [20%, 64%]).
The 'EC vs CH' effect from Phase 15 didn't fully reproduce — within the noise band, but the magnitude was overstated.

Combined 3-arm experiment (control vs EC vs CH, joint judging) wasn't run; we ran two separate vs-control comparisons. A future N=20+ joint experiment with all three responses judged together would be cleaner.
verdict: WIN — the technical-prompt story flips. With the neutral wrapper, imagination injection is net-positive (or at least neutral) on technical work. The shipping defaults (engineering routing → neutral wrapper) are validated by data, not just intuition.
next_steps: Phase 17 — per-prompt routing for decision-shaped prompts (running now). The legacy-deletion 87% EC result strongly suggests decision-shaped prompts deserve dreams wrapper even on engineering agents.
Phase 19 (suggested): replicate Phase 16 with the expanded Phase 18 library (30 seeds vs 15) to see if larger library changes outcomes.

Phase 20 (suggested): combined 3-arm experiment where Sonnet judges all three responses jointly (control + EC + CH) rather than two pairwise comparisons. Cleaner statistical handling of the joint claim.
